originality.rationale: Six targeted semantic searches of published mathematical results and a comparison against related graph-heat theorems found no statement implying the exact time-dependent one-edge-conductance C4 Lipschitz norm, its w=3 contractivity transition, and its sharp nonattained 3/2 singular envelope. The primary Veysseire theorem supplies the general W1 contraction mechanism but not the needed graph-specific formulas; Lin–Lu–Yau treat a normalized unweighted model. The inference is best-knowledge original, not proof of database completeness; an unindexed analytic computation remains a risk.

value.rationale: The smallest Cartesian square admits a minimal one-rate symmetry break. The result gives the full exact stability profile, detects an exact one-edge rate threshold at w=3, identifies the sharp exponential contraction rate with a kink at w=1, and proves a nonattained 3/2 transient envelope with noncommuting high-conductance and short-time limits. These answer natural quantitative contraction questions not determined by general graph-curvature bounds.
